newsitem.title: USA: MOTOR RACING-RAIN POSTPONES INDIANAPOLIS 500 AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-RAIN POSTPONES INDIANAPOLIS 500 AGAIN.

text.p: For the second successive day, the 81st running of the Indianapolis 500 was postponed after heavy rain soaked the Indianapolis Motor Speedway.
The race, which was originally scheduled for Sunday, did get underway on Monday, but was halted after 15 of the 200 laps had been run.
After a rain delay of some three hours, the decision was made to again postpone the race until Wednesday at noon EDT (1600 GMT), weather permitting.
"We made every effort to run today but we came up short," said Indianapolis Motor Speedway chief steward Keith Ward. "There was absolutely no way we can get the track in shape to run."
The last time the famed Indy 500 was postponed by rain on Sunday and Monday was 1986, when officials opted to push the race to the following Saturday.
"We will go tomorrow or the next day when we can get it done," added Ward, who said the race would not be put off until next weekend due to a scheduling conflict.
When the red flag came out, Tony Stewart led the field into the pits with Arie Luyendyk, Robbie Buhl, Robby Gordon and rookie Vincenzo Sospiri of Italy running in the top five.
Stewart was able to overtake polesitter Luyendyk at the end of the first lap, becoming the first driver to lead the opening lap of the race in his first two years in the event.

Ward said the race would re-start with a minimum of two laps run under a yellow caution flag. The cars will start in the order in which they came into the pits Monday. Cars that were out of the race at the time it was halted will not be allowed back in.
The day got off to a rocky beginning even before the race officially started Monday when a three-car crash on the formation lap wiped out the entire fifth row of the 35-car field.

The cars driven by Brazilian Affonso Giaffone, Swede Kenny Brack and Frenchman Stephan Gregoire -- all of which were to start from the fifth row on the grid -- smashed into the wall at the entrance to turn four as the field was getting set to take the green flag.
"Everybody's angry, but nobody knows what happened," Gregoire said. "Giaffone touched me, and then I went right into the wall."
Said Brack: "I really don't know what happened. I got knocked out from behind. I was keeping a level pace with the cars in front. I would like to see a replay."
Two of the three entries from the Blueprint Racing team also will miss the race as rookies Claude Bourbonnais of Canada and Sam Schmidt saw their new engines fail.
The third member of the team, Jim Guthrie, is in the race but will start seven laps behind the leaders after battling overheating problems.

Italian Alessandro Zampedri, who was making his comeback from a horrible wreck on the last lap of the 1996 Indy 500 that left him with badly broken legs and feet, was also out of the race with mechanical problems.
More than $8 million in prizes are posted for the event at the world's most famous oval race track with the winner being assured of a purse in excess of $1 million.
